newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, ACCESS gains on AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, ACCESS gains on AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, pressured by bearish views on storage and some technical selling, mostly ended lower Wednesday in a sluggish session, then gained slightly on ACCESS after the AGAs.
March skidded 10.8 cents to close at $2.438 per million British thermal units, then climbed to $2.45 on ACCESS after the stock report. April settled 10.1 cents lower at $2.156.

"The market may have discounted the AGA number and sold off a little too hard earlier, so they're buying it back on ACCESS," said one East Coast trader, noting eastern region stocks were still at a sizeable surplus to last year.

AGA said U.S. gas stocks fell last week by 150 bcf, in line with average expecatations, with overall stocks about even with year-ago. But the report showed eastern stocks were still 147 bcf, or 18 percent, above last year's levels.

Despite forecasts for fairly cold Midwest and Northeast weather, traders said relatively mild temperatures in Texas and the South coupled with comfortable inventories in the East were likely to make any rally difficult to sustain.

And while technical traders said the market was oversold and due for an upside correction, they agreed March's close below trendline support and the double bottom likely means more selling ahead. Next support was seen at the December low of $2.35 and then in the $2.12 area. Resistance remained at $2.70 and $2.80.

In the cash, February Gulf Coast prices were off five cents or more Wednesday to the mid-to-high $2.80s. Feb Midcon pipes also were lost about five cents to the mid-$2.70s. New York city gate gas for Feb delivery was quoted little changed in the $3.60s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell 4.4 cents to $2.194. NYMEX said an estimated 28,588 Hub contracts traded, down from Tuesday's revised tally of 23,367.
NYMEX Feb Alberta natgas expired 12 cents lower at $2.12, while Feb Permian went off the board at $2.55, down five cents. NYMEX said 12 Alberta contracts and 14 Permian lots changed hands.

On the KCBT, March finished 17 cents lower at $2.14, while deferreds ended down by six to 13 cents. The East/West spread widened by 6.2 cents to 29.8 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 118 contracts traded, down from Tuesday's total of 731.
